chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Skipping kindergarten recess for the Palmetto swimming hole
summary: Asked where he learned it, Green tells of leaving school grounds with other children on his first kindergarten day for the Palmetto swimming hole in Georgia.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, Chuck, wheredid you learn to do that step?
Well, I was a mascot, you see.
Well, I was pinch-hitting mascot for some kind of dalmation, they call it, you see, and I was trying

to pay a debt back, you see. My life got saved accidentally, you know. I almost got adopted by the 13th wonder of the world, which is Jumbo the Elephant. I thought it was an out house -- I didn't know, you see.
Now, this is the truth -- don't think that I don't have no ski poles because it sounds like -- it's mysterious, you see.
Could you explain it with a little more detail?
Well, the detail is, it was my first day at the children's school, you see. It's called kindergarten --
This is tape number 18 of Chuck Green. So, you were just saying you were in kindergarten describing how you learned the hobbler.

Yes. Well, we had just finished recess. Now, the teacher -- our teacher would say, "Class will now be dismissed for recess for an hour of (unintelligible) recess." And we used to come out and she'd say, "But you must not leave the school grounds." She said playgrounds. So, boys will be boys, you know, trying to separate the sheep from the goats. They said, "Let's go to Palmetto." "Palmetto? Where is that?" So, we go down to Palm Grove, a long street, we got to go through the path, and we come to the swimming hole -- that's

Palmetto. "Me, too," we'd say. "I'm going to go with her. She can't swim." "Yes, she can, too -- not in the same water with you." So, here we go. Now, weren't supposed to do that -- it was naughty. We weren't supposed to go off the school play ground. But, here we go -- we go a short cut. We go -- there was about nine of us -- little ones, you know, so we got to go and it looked like we got further and further away from the school. I have to laugh because I still get the picture. When we arrived down there, see, we're going to Walzer bridge, and this stream -- what you would call it, a creek, was going up through Palmetto, see. Palmetto is a swimming hole. But I don't know what you could say about him (unintelligible) you see all kinds -- guard was very busy at that place. Children can find some places like that, you know. So, when we gets there it's very peaceful, you know. So, we didn't have on no shoes anyhow, we was barefoot, you know. So, when we get there one says, "Look here, look there -- see that? There's the babies." (unintelligible) So, we says, "You going to go in?" It's still peaceful, you know. So, one of them takes up some kind of a hard piece of clay, you know, and skips it across the water. So, those schools of minnows, you know, they would go into the shadows of the waters of Palmetto -- see, that's the swimming hole. Now, you can either jump in feet first or get on the -- like the bank -- the embankment, you know, and climb down and touch the water with your bare foot to see if it's cool enough or -- you know. We still talk bout the Pretty Foot, you see.
